sections.label: Site audit
paragraphs: I audited the existing site and mapped what worked and what didn't. Looked at how competitors structured their sites and where Rokoko could differentiate. Talked to users across different segments to understand what each audience actually came looking for.

sections.label: The opportunity
paragraphs: The competitive analysis showed most motion capture companies didn't serve diverse audiences well. That was the opportunity.

sections.label: Three zones, one brand
paragraphs: The site needed three distinct zones that felt like one brand. Marketing for discovery and storytelling. Knowledge base for support and learning. E-commerce for sales. Each would have different visual density and interaction patterns, but all three would feel like Rokoko.

sections.label: Information architecture
paragraphs: I mapped out the information architecture carefully. Product overviews. Industry solutions. Community resources. Support docs. Shop. Each section had a clear purpose and a logical entry point.

sections.label: Modular template system
paragraphs: I created modular templates so the marketing team could rapidly build new pages without design support. Homepage, product pages, industry solutions, user stories, pricing, help articles, shop product pages. Each template was flexible but on-brand.

sections.label: Design system documentation
paragraphs: The design system documented everything. Components, color rules, typography, interaction patterns, and responsive behavior. This made it possible for the Webflow developer to build without constant back-and-forth.

sections.label: Visual language
paragraphs: Visual exploration established the look and feel. The new brand was bold and modern. The website needed to match that energy while staying functional and fast.
